title: toolcall stability scorer and auto-unwind playbook for canary/A-B/shadow rollouts
creator: Ava Martin
description: Create a deterministic scoring system and operational playbook that evaluates function-call / structured-output compatibility during canary, A/B, and shadow traffic rollouts. The goal is to detect subtle contract regressions (argument shape changes, required->optional flips, field renames) and emergent runtime mismatches (runtime invocation errors, signature mismatches, semantic output drop) and automatically unwind unsafe rollouts when safety thresholds are violated.
motivation: We continue to see production regressions caused by model variants that change function-call shapes or structured outputs in ways that break downstream orchestrators. Existing diffs and schema drift alerts are noisy and not combined into a single operational signal. Engineering needs a single, explainable score and a clear auto-unwind policy that integrates with Console rollouts and Dedicated routing so we can safely accelerate canaries with fewer manual checkpoints.
proposal: Build a Toolcall Stability Scorer (TSS) that ingests shadow and canary telemetry (signature mismatch rate, schema delta magnitude, invocation error rate, latency regression, semantic task-level quality delta) and emits a 0-1 stability score. Wire TSS into the rollout service: every canary interval the orchestrator fetches the score and enforces policies. Add an auto-unwind runbook that escalates in two phases (soft pause + notify, then automatic revert) with audit logs and a Slack/Sentry gating path.
stability_score_formula: score = clamp(0,1, 0.40*signature_compat + 0.25*(1 - normalized_schema_delta) + 0.20*(1 - normalized_invocation_error) + 0.10*(1 - latency_regression_norm) + 0.05*(semantic_match_score_norm)). All submetrics normalized to 0..1. Signatures carry the highest weight because they are typically breaking.
gating_thresholds_and_policy: Canary pass threshold: score >= 0.90 for 10min rolling window with <0.05% signature mismatch. Soft-fail: 0.85 <= score < 0.90 triggers canary pause + PM/Engineering notification. Auto-unwind: score < 0.85 for a sustained 15 minutes or signature mismatch > 0.2% for 5 minutes triggers automatic rollback to previous model variant + traffic reroute to fallback. For A/B experiments we require both cohort scores >= 0.90 and no asymmetric signature mismatch >0.1%.
schema_checks:
- Structural superset check (new model output must be a superset or backward-compatible mapping of previous schema).
- Required field introduction flagged as breaking.
- Parameter type widening/narrowing rules documented (e.g., string->string|null allowed, string->int flagged).
- Field rename heuristics (Levenshtein + doc mapping) produce a suspected rename confidence; low confidence contributes to schema_delta.
storage_and_retention: Keep full diff payloads in the shadow sink for 30 days for forensics. Aggregate metrics stored in metrics DB for 1 year. Detailed per-invocation diffs sampled at 1% but increased to 100% for incidents and during first 60 minutes of a canary.
implementation_steps: Instrument runtime to emit structured diff blobs (old_output vs new_output) and normalized signature comparison per invocation (done)
Build TSS microservice: scoring logic, historical windowing, backfills (3 days), and API for rollout service
Add gating integration in rollout-orchestrator: poll TSS every 1m during canary and A/B ramps
Implement auto-unwind action: rollback API call + traffic reroute + audit event
Console UI: show TSS score timeline, top schema diffs, and one-click abort/approve for canaries
End-to-end test harness: simulator to inject controlled diffs and verify playbook behavior
Document playbook and update runbooks (PagerDuty, Slack, Incident template)
acceptance_criteria:
- TSS API returns a 0..1 stability score and breakdown of submetrics for any active rollout.
- Rollout orchestrator pauses/continues/rolls back according to thresholds without manual intervention in test harness.
- Console displays per-canary TSS timeline and top-3 breaking diffs.
- Alerts and audit logs created on soft-fail and auto-unwind actions.
- No false-positive auto-unwinds in controlled 100-simulated-canary test suite (target <1% false trigger).
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring functions, integration tests between runtime -> shadow sink -> TSS -> orchestrator, staged e2e in staging with synthetic models that introduce each class of break (signature change, new required field, type narrowing). Run 50 canary sims overnight to validate thresholds. Post-deploy runbook drill with on-call engineer.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable TSS in read-only mode for all canaries (no auto-unwind) for 2 weeks, collect baseline scores. Phase 2 (canary experiments): enable soft-fail notifications for internal teams and escalate by invite-only projects. Phase 3 (opt-in auto-unwind): enable automatic reverts for internal projects with strict SLIs. Phase 4 (global): flip auto-unwind default on for tenant-guarded canaries after 90% stability in Phase 3.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana dashboard: tss.score.percentile, signature_mismatch_rate, schema_delta_by_field. Create slack channel #rollout-safety and send summarized daily digests. PagerDuty escalation only after auto-unwind + customer-impact detected.
operational_playbook: 1) Soft-fail: Notify owner + post detailed diff to #rollout-safety, 2) Owner has 15 min to acknowledge and provide rationale in Console, 3) If no action or score continues to drop -> orchestrator triggers auto-unwind and opens incident with attached diff artifacts, 4) Post-mortem within 48 hours if auto-unwind impacted production traffic.
open_questions: Q1: Should semantic_match_score come from model-provided evaluation or from a downstream golden-set reranker? (tradeoff: latency vs signal quality)
Q2: What sampling rate for storing full diffs balances cost vs investigability? Proposal: 1% default, 100% first 60 minutes of canary.
Q3: How to handle multi-model toolchains where caller and callee are both changing? Proposal: require coordinated rollout tickets and disable auto-unwind for coordinated low-risk rollouts.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-sensitive thresholds cause unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: read-only baseline period, tune weights after 2 weeks of signals.
Risk: Attack surface for privacy-sensitive diffs -> Mitigation: redact PII at ingestion and enforce KMS encryption for stored diffs.
Risk: Coupling TSS to rollout orchestrator creates single-point-of-failure -> Mitigation: orchestrator has fallback to manual-gated mode when TSS is unavailable.
